RECREATIONAL_GROW.question: Is it legal for adults to grow cannabis in the state of New Mexico?
RECREATIONAL_GROW.gov_section: A single adult, 21 years of age or older, can grow up to 12 plants at their private residence, but no more than six (6) plants can be mature, flowering plants. A household with multiple adults can have no more than 12 mature plants total.

sourceNotes: The official cannabis homepage used for this walk is https://www.rld.nm.gov/cannabis/cannabis-in-new-mexico/, set on 2026-09-08. That page is the Cannabis Control Division's Cannabis in New Mexico overview on rld.nm.gov. Yes and Knows answers adult possession. Adult Use answers adult purchase limits and medical patient purchase and home possession. Personal Use of Cannabis answers adult home cultivation of up to six mature plants, which is also how a patient 21 or older may grow. The FAQs answer the public-consumption ban, licensed consumption lounges, and medical sales to cardholders. Citations that had been on nmonesource.com and nmhealth.org were replaced because those hosts are not the requested source and this host already answers the questions. The homepage still links to nmhealth.org/about/mcp/svcs/ as the Department of Health medical cannabis patient program, and to nmonesource.com for the Cannabis Regulation Act and the Lynn and Erin Compassionate Use Act; both hosts were already confirmed official on 2026-08-31 and the same .gov links were still present on 2026-09-08. Fetch with browser headers returns 200 and the excerpts are in the HTML, so these rows do not need a browser.
